$what: connection:press-fit-sole-foot — the measured fit between the TPU sole's socket and the foot cap's plug, from cecad.meshfeatures.intervals ray-cast calipers and cecad.meshslice sections on Pollen's sole_left.stl and foot_left.stl (metres, scale 1000), 2026-09-02, ce-designs/microduck lane T

sides.mirror: the right side is the same joint on part:microduck-sole-right / part:microduck-foot-right; the two meshes mirror about x

frame: Pollen's shared mesh frame for the left ankle group: x heel 30 .. toe 70, y -12 .. 42, z up. sole_left bbox z -31.2493 .. -18.3419; foot_left bbox z -29.2509 .. -12.3419.

section_mm.how: the foot plug's outer wall is a vertical prism: cecad.meshslice z-sections at -18.342, -18.5, -19.0, -20.0, -22.0 and -24.0 all read exactly u 31.6000..68.4000, v -9.9000..39.9000

clearance.how: ray-cast calipers (cecad.meshfeatures.intervals) run through BOTH meshes on the same line: 54 y-lines at z -19/-20/-21/-22/-23/-24 x x 34..66 step 4, and 21 x-lines at z -19/-21/-23 x y -6..37. Each station yields two gaps (the -side and the +side).
clearance.reading: ZERO CLEARANCE. 150 measured gaps span -0.0020 .. +0.0020 mm about a mean of -0.000007 mm — the two walls are the SAME surface to within the 0.002 mm the decimated STL can express. This is not a fit with an allowance; it is a coincident surface pair, and no press force can be derived from it.

socket_wall_mm.how: the first caliper interval on the sole side at each station
socket_wall_mm.plateau: 2.1000 on the long (y) walls at every x from 38 to 62; 1.8210-2.0480 on the short (x) walls

socket_depth_mm.rim_how: the sole's own bbox maximum; meshslice finds 0 segments at z -18.3419 and 659 at z -18.3421
socket_depth_mm.why_it_varies: the sole's outer floor slopes toe-to-heel (the `ground` interface on part:microduck-sole-left measures 0.087 over the footprint); the inner floor follows it at a constant 1.9990-2.0010 mm of TPU, so the socket is deeper at the heel.

floor_thickness_mm.reading: 2.000 +/- 0.001 mm of TPU under the whole plug — the sole's `foot_socket` interface states 2.000 +/- 0.005 from its own 27x31 floor grid, and these nine independent stations agree.

rib_landing.note: the foot's ribs reach 0.2539 mm BELOW the sole's inner floor at the deepest station measured (x 35, y 15). Whether that is interference to be squeezed out of the TPU or a modelling overlap in the visual meshes is CANNOT DETERMINE from the meshes: the two parts are separate rigid geoms in the MJCF and nothing there resolves the overlap.

corner_radii.socket: R3.4 back / R4.9 front — MEASURED in part:microduck-sole-left's own cad/interfaces.json (corner circle fits at z -19)
corner_radii.plug: R3.45 back / R4.89 front — MEASURED in part:microduck-foot-left's own cad/interfaces.json
corner_radii.not_re-measured_here: lane T's own corner circle fits at z -19.0 and -22.0 were REJECTED, not published: the fit windows catch the internal ribs as well as the wall and the residual mean came out 0.13-1.05 mm, which is a worse instrument than the one the part folders already used. A worse measurement does not replace a better one.

fasteners.how: cecad.meshfeatures.cylinders on sole_left.stl finds no hole of any diameter through the socket wall or floor; the only screw in the ankle group is the single M2 at (x 50.0000, y 4.5020) that hangs the FOOT from the ankle (part:microduck-ankle-left `foot_screw` -> part:microduck-foot-left `ankle_screw`, connection:threaded-m2), and it does not pass through the sole.
